name: Port of Boston
text: A deep-water container and cruise port. Pilots board outbound ships here.

name: Port of New York (Ambrose Channel)
text: The busiest harbour on the coast. Expect crossing traffic and impatient pilots.

name: Naval Station Newport
text: A naval base at the mouth of Narragansett Bay. They will answer hails promptly.

name: St. George's Harbour, Bermuda
text: A small, busy mid-ocean port. Last fuel and fresh water for a long way.

name: Horta, Faial (Azores)
text: A yacht harbour and the Atlantic's crossroads. Every ocean sailor stops here.

name: Ponta Delgada, São Miguel (Azores)
text: The Azores' main commercial port and a supply base for the Ridge.

name: Funchal, Madeira
text: A cruise and cargo port on the eastern edge of the chart.

name: Meridian Habitat
text: A permanent deep-water colony of about four hundred people on a seamount, started by former OERA contractors. Independent and proud of it.
reply: Meridian Habitat. Welcome, Aqua Nova. Please announce your approach. Our docking arms are narrow and our patience is wide.

name: Deepcut Station
text: A nodule-mining station on the abyssal plain. Dredge ships work the floor for miles around and do not like visitors in the pattern.
reply: Deepcut Station. State your business. Do not enter the dredge pattern. You are not insured.

name: Lucky Strike Sulphide Works
text: Seafloor massive sulphide mining on a live vent field. A co-op runs it, and their safety board is strict.
reply: Lucky Strike Works. Aqua Nova, welcome. Keep to the marked corridor. The vents are hot and the miners are tired.

name: Rainbow Camp
text: A rival claim on the Rainbow vent field, run on a thin budget and thick paperwork.
reply: Rainbow Camp. Who is this? We have no visitors scheduled. State your registry.

name: Sable Shelf-1 Platform
text: An oil platform on the outer shelf, a supply stop for the fishing fleet and the oil crews.
reply: Sable Shelf One. Aqua Nova, we have you. Keep your distance from the risers, please.

name: Concord Station Echo
text: A foreign seabed listening post. Officially it does not exist.
reply: This is a restricted area. Aqua Nova, change course immediately.

name: Sargasso Haven
text: A drifting anchorage in the weed where the Black Tide Syndicate trades. Unconfirmed. Ships that go in do not always come out.

name: Hydrographer Canyon Sanctuary
text: A protected canyon system. Fishing is banned, which is why the poachers come.

name: Block Canyon Closed Area
text: A seasonal closure to let the fish recover. Patrols are thin.

name: Andrea Doria
text: The liner that sank after a collision in fog in 1956. A famous, dangerous dive. Her hull is a magnet for fishing nets and curious divers.

name: USS San Diego
text: An armoured cruiser that struck a mine in 1918, the largest US warship lost in the First World War.

name: U-853
text: A German U-boat sunk off Block Island in the last days of the Second World War.

name: SS Portland
text: A paddle steamer lost with everyone aboard in the Portland Gale of 1898.

name: Hudson Canyon
text: The largest submarine canyon on the US east coast. Its head holds cold, nutrient-rich water and a lot of life.

name: Bear Seamount
text: The first of the New England Seamounts. Corals, sponges and a ring of hungry fish.

name: Kelvin Seamount
text: Part of the New England Seamount chain. A good place to see how the deep sea hugs a mountain.

name: Baltimore Canyon Seep
text: A cold seep where methane leaks from the slope and mussels feed on it in the dark.

name: Lost City Hydrothermal Field
text: Towers of white carbonate rise like cathedral spires from a vent field that has run for tens of thousands of years.

name: Menez Gwen Vent Field
text: A shallow vent field on the Ridge, home to dense beds of mussels and shrimp.
